mathgap.title: Direct count assignment at point of mention
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly gives a count for a person, set that person's current count to the given number at that point in the narrative. This count may later change due to transfers or other operations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence of the form "X has N <objects>" appears without any relational clause.
mathgap.example: Treating a direct count as a permanent final value and ignoring later transfers that modify it.

mathgap.title: Directionality of more/fewer statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret "X has N more than Y" as X = Y + N, and "X has N fewer than Y" as X = Y - N. Preserve the order of the names as given.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a sentence contains the phrases "more than" or "fewer than" linking two people.
mathgap.example: Writing Y = X + N instead of X = Y + N, thereby swapping the direction of the relationship.

mathgap.title: Split‑all handling
mathgap.principle: When a person splits all of their items equally among two recipients, each recipient receives half of the giver's current count and the giver's count becomes zero.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says "X splits all the <objects> she owns equally among Y and Z".
mathgap.example: Giving each recipient half of the original amount but forgetting to set the giver's count to zero.

mathgap.title: Sequential transfer handling with updated counts
mathgap.principle: Process each transfer in the order it appears: subtract the transferred amount from the giver's current count and add it to the receiver's current count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence of the form "X gives N <objects> to Y" is encountered.
mathgap.example: Applying a later transfer using the giver's original count instead of the count after earlier transfers.

mathgap.title: Substitution of known signed differences into signed difference equalities
mathgap.principle: If a signed difference (e.g., X‑Y) is already known numerically, substitute its value into any equality that contains it to simplify and solve for the remaining unknowns.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When solving an equation of the form (A‑B) = (C‑D) and one side is already determined.
mathgap.example: Leaving an equation with a known difference unevaluated, missing an easy simplification step.

mathgap.title: Chronological evaluation of statements
mathgap.principle: Read and apply statements in the exact order they appear, because later statements refer to counts after earlier updates (transfers, increases, etc.).
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any problem that contains multiple statements affecting the same variables.
mathgap.example: Solving all equations simultaneously without respecting the order, causing contradictions with later transfer effects.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: For a clause "If X has more than N items, X will transfer their items to Y", evaluate the condition using X's current count at that point; if true, set X to zero and add its entire count to Y.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement contains an "If ... has more than" condition followed by a transfer.
mathgap.example: Always performing the transfer regardless of whether the condition is satisfied, or never performing it.

mathgap.title: Target variable dependency analysis
mathgap.principle: Trace which equations and variables directly or indirectly affect the target variable, and ignore statements that involve unrelated persons. Solve the reduced system to obtain the answer efficiently.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem contains many extraneous statements that do not influence the asked person.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve the entire large system including irrelevant variables, leading to wasted effort and possible errors.

mathgap.title: Signed difference handling with trivial equality detection
mathgap.principle: If a signed‑difference equality has identical expressions on both sides (e.g., (X‑Y) = (X‑Y)), recognize it as a trivial identity that provides no new information and can be ignored.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a signed‑difference equation where the left‑hand and right‑hand expressions are syntactically the same.
mathgap.example: Treating a trivial equality as a meaningful constraint and trying to solve for variables from it.

mathgap.title: Multiplicative increase handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "The number of X increases by K times", interpret it as multiplying X's current count by K (X = X * K), not as adding K.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence contains the phrase "increase(s) by ... times".
mathgap.example: Interpreting "increase by 3 times" as X = X + 3 instead of X = X * 3.

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences or swapping term order
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model confuses the signed nature of "difference between X and Y" with an absolute distance and may reverse the order of the terms.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Keep the order exactly as written and treat the expression as X - Y, not |X - Y| or Y - X.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model processes transfers independently of their position, losing the cumulative effect of earlier changes.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer in the order it appears, updating the giver's and receiver's counts before processing the next statement.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: Direct count statements are taken as immutable final values, overlooking later operations that modify those counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat a direct count as the current value at that moment; later transfers can increase or decrease it.

mathgap.why_it_happens: Conditional clauses are overlooked, causing the model to either always apply or never apply the transfer.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Evaluate the condition using the current count at that point; only perform the transfer if the condition holds.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting multiplicative increase statements as additive
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrasing "increase by K times" is read as an addition of K rather than a multiplication by K.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Recognize that "increase by K times" means multiply the existing count by K (X = X * K).
